sections.heading: Cláusulas relativas especificativas (Defining)
sections.body: Una cláusula relativa especificativa o definitoria (*defining relative clause*) aporta información esencial para identificar con precisión de qué persona o cosa se habla. **No lleva comas**. En este tipo de cláusulas se puede sustituir 'who' o 'which' por **'that'**, y el pronombre relativo puede omitirse si funciona como objeto (*'The book (that) I bought is great'*).

sections.heading: Cláusulas relativas explicativas (Non-defining)
sections.body: Una cláusula relativa explicativa (*non-defining relative clause*) añade información complementaria y no esencial sobre un sustantivo que ya ha sido identificado. **Siempre va entre comas**, **nunca usa 'that'** (solo *who, which, whose, where*) y el pronombre relativo **nunca puede omitirse** (*'My father, who is a doctor, lives in Lima'*).

examples.english: The woman who called is my manager.
examples.note: Especificativa (defining): aclara exactamente qué mujer llamó; sin comas.

examples.english: My manager, who called earlier, wants to meet.
examples.note: Explicativa (non-defining): información extra sobre el sujeto; va entre comas.

examples.english: The film (that) I recommended was great.
examples.note: Pronombre relativo en posición de objeto: se puede omitir.

examples.english: Shakespeare, whose plays are still performed, was born in 1564.

exercises.instruction: Indica si cada cláusula es especificativa (D) o explicativa (ND).
items: The house where I grew up has been demolished. ___ (D / ND)
My father, who is a doctor, works at the local hospital. ___ (D / ND)
The report that you submitted had several errors. ___ (D / ND)
Lima, which is the capital of Peru, is a fascinating city. ___ (D / ND)

quiz.question: Which of the following sentences correctly uses a non-defining relative clause?
options: My car that is red is parked outside.
My car, which is red, is parked outside.
My car which is red is parked outside.
My car, that is red, is parked outside.
quiz.explanation: Non-defining relative clauses provide extra non-essential information and must be enclosed in commas and use 'which' (never 'that').
